original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.
Extending a source-count census without naming a supplier/interface decision it could change; audit #2973 pruning concerns before relying on the affected predecessor exclusions.

actual_scope: Classify all radical two-role right-vector targets over split square-zero K-algebras; prove exact cost 2 or unreachable and a closed binary count for every radical dimension.
scope_change_reason: Take the explicit singular-target open question of PR4601 rather than extend the native connector alphabet. This is a formal-alphabet side result, not supplier admission.
bottleneck_link: Separates reachable singular formal interfaces from targets no longer word can implement; native conversion and complete supplier costs remain unknown.
stop_rule: Stop at the first verified common-zero criterion and its count; do not extend to higher nilpotency, more roles or a native implementation.
evidence: README proof; complete literal two-factor images for radical dimensions 0..3; independent 511-subset counting polynomial; first-zero transition and rejection controls.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Which additional obstruction appears when J cubed is zero but J squared is nonzero?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Decides whether longer words enlarge the radical image once first-order truncation fails.
open_questions.first_step: Expand the first zero residue event over F2[x,y]/(x,y)^3.
open_questions.blocked_by: Products of radical entries survive; no second-order invariant is supplied.

open_questions.question: What is the closed reachability count over every finite field Fq?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Turns the arbitrary-field criterion into an exact distribution beyond binary coefficients.
open_questions.first_step: Count rank-one-free subspaces of M2(Fq) and their ordered spanning tuples.
open_questions.blocked_by: The binary plane count does not classify all higher-field subspaces.
